parts.text: A student investigates the refraction of light through a transparent block. Fig. 3.1 shows the transparent block ABCD on the student’s ray-trace sheet. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Draw a normal at the centre of side AB . Continue the normal so that it reaches the bottom of the ray-trace sheet. Label the normal NL . • Label the point Q where NL crosses AB . [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • Draw a line EF parallel to CD and 2.0 cm below CD . • Label the point J where NL crosses EF . • Draw a line GH parallel to CD and 7.0 cm below CD . • Label the point K where NL crosses GH . [1]

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text: EF and GH at 2.0 cm and 5.0 cm

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Draw a line PQ at an angle i = 30° to the normal and on the left-hand side of the normal above the block. [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(i)
ms.text: i = 30° ± 2° to the left of normal and above the block

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student places two pins P 1 and P 2 on line PQ . Fig. 3.1 is not drawn full size. Suggest a suitable distance apart for pins P 1 and P 2 in this type of experiment. distance apart ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(ii)
ms.text: P1P2 distance at least 5.0 cm but not greater than 15 cm

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student observes the images of P 1 and P 2 through side CD of the block. She adjusts her line of sight until the images of P 1 and P 2 appear one behind the other. She places a pin P 3 on line EF and a pin P 4 on line GH so that P 3 , and the images of P 1 and P 2 seen through the block, appear behind pin P 4 .

ms.label: 3(d)(ii)
ms.text: b between 5.2 and 5.6 cm or 52 and 56 mm, and correct unit seen in (i) or (ii) and not contradicted

ms.label: 3(d)(iii)
ms.text:
b / a value quoted with no unit
b / a lies within range 2.00 to 2.50

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
One from:
View bases of pins
Pins at least 5cm apart
Ensure pins are vertical

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) A student plans to test the suggestion that, in this experiment, b a is a constant for all possible values of i . List suitable values of i that the student could use. ............................................................................................................................................. [2]

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text:
At least 4 additional values, all < 90°
Range at least 30°
